schedule.label: Automatic backup of this server
schedule.help: Vespry silently re-exports this server on the chosen schedule. It picks up only the new messages since the last successful run, across all accessible channels.
large_run.title: Large export ahead
large_run.body: About {n} messages estimated. Vespry will work through them in batches of 100.
large_run.detail: Depending on the number of messages and media, this can take from a few minutes to several hours: Discreet pace takes regular breaks.
large_run.background_ok: Keep a Discord tab open, Vespry goes through it. If you close it, the export pauses and resumes on its own the next time Discord is open.
tip.encryption: Protect your zip with a password (AES-256). Without one, the archive comes out unencrypted and readable by anyone.
tip.schedule: Vespry re-runs an incremental export of the whole server at the chosen cadence, automatically. The export starts as soon as a Discord tab is open. Keeps your backup fresh.
tip.formats: JSON for AI agents, HTML to read it back, CSV for Excel, TXT for grep. You can tick more than one.
tip.period: Limit the export to a date range. Speeds up large servers a lot.
tip.partition: If a channel has more than N messages, Vespry splits the file into chunks. Useful for huge HTML files that lag when opened.
tip.incremental: Vespry only fetches messages posted since your last export of the same server. Much faster once the initial backup is done.
tip.schema_optin: Discord sometimes changes its API. If enabled, Vespry sends only the names of newly detected fields (never your message content, never your token) so the extension can be updated.
privacy.schema_optin: Help keep Vespry up to date when Discord changes its API

tos.title: Read this before your first export
tos.account: Vespry reads your history with your own Discord account, from the open discord.com tab. Discord’s terms of service forbid automating a user account.
tos.sanctions: Since March 2026, Discord has been penalizing accounts that export their history with tools like this one: forced logout, temporary restriction, suspension for repeat cases.
tos.measures: To limit that risk, Vespry goes through the Discord client in your page (same headers, same cookies), reads at a human pace with regular breaks, and stops at the first signal from Discord: verification, refusal or a request to slow down.
tos.no_guarantee: This lowers the risk; it does not remove it. No tool can guarantee your account won’t be penalized.
tos.private: Vespry is made for your own data: your servers, your direct messages, your archives. Not for harvesting other people’s conversations.
pace.label: Pace
pace.help: Discreet: 1.5 to 3.5 s between requests, one channel at a time, a break of about ten minutes every 40 to 50 min. Normal: roughly twice as fast, same breaks.
pace.warn_body: Normal pace is roughly twice as fast, so it sends twice as many requests per minute. That is closer to what Discord flags as a bot.
pace.warn_failed: The engine didn’t take the change. Try again in a moment.
purge.risk: Deleting messages in bulk is what Discord watches most closely. At Discreet pace, Vespry deletes one message every 3 to 6 s and stops at the first refusal.
stop.auth: Discord session expired. Log in again, then click Resume.
stop.refused: Discord refused a request (verification or block). Wait a few hours before resuming.
stop.blocked: Discord returned a protection page. Wait a few hours before resuming.
stop.rate-limited: Discord is asking to slow down. Wait at least an hour before resuming.
stop.no-tab: Open Discord in a tab to continue: it resumes automatically.
stop.no-client: Discord hasn’t finished loading: it resumes automatically.
idx.title: Discord export — {guild}
idx.read_html: `html/<channel>.html` — readable page, Discord-style. Open it in a browser.
idx.read_json: `json/<channel>.json` — one file per channel, messages in chronological order. Each message has `id`, `timestamp`, `author`, `content`, `attachments`, `embeds`, `reactions`, `mentions`, `message_reference` (= a reply to an original message). Downloaded media carry a `localPath` field.
idx.read_media: `media/` images · `video/` videos · `audio/` audio · `files/` other files — sorted by channel.
